subject: Order Form — binding sequence and true-up playbook for Exhibit pricing
messages:
From: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@novus.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novus.health>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit pricing — sequencing & true-up questions

Sean,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our procurement team reviewed Exhibit pricing (the caps / floors and the true-up timing) and we have three narrow clarifying asks before legal will sign:

1) Binding sequence: we need explicit language describing which schedule becomes binding if there is a conflict between the Order Schedule (worksheet) and Exhibit pricing (Exhibit E). Currently the draft is silent and our finance team insists on a deterministic rule.

2) True-up cadence: Novus prefers quarterly true-ups pro-rated on usage rather than an annual true-up — can Redwood confirm operational support and whether that changes the floor/commit calculation?

3) Billing mapping: we surfaced a scenario where usage spans two SKU families during a migration window; we want a fallback for invoice mapping so we are not double-billed for tokens during transition.

I attached a short spreadsheet with an example month (OrderSchedule_Worksheet_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm Redwood's position and suggest language we can include in the next redline?

Appreciate it — happy to take a 20-min call if it's easier.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Levin
Sr. Procurement Manager, Novus Health

Attachments: OrderSchedule_Worksheet_v2.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Levin <sarah.levin@novus.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit pricing — sequencing & true-up questions

Thanks Sarah — this is helpful and totally reasonable to resolve before signature. Short answers up-front:

- Binding sequence: our standard is "Order of Precedence" in Section 1.3 of the Order Form, but I agree it should be explicit for Exhibit E. Markus, can we propose a short clause that the Order Schedule governs for SKU-specific mechanics and Exhibit E governs pricing guardrails (caps/floors) unless the parties explicitly note an exception?

- True-up cadence: we support quarterly true-ups operationally, but it affects the commit math (quarterly pro-ration will tighten the effective floor vs annual). Karthik, can you confirm the billing/commit impact and whether we can preserve the same floor by adjusting the prorated calculation?

- Billing mapping/migration: Marissa, please review the attached worksheet and propose a fallback mapping (e.g., last-good mapping per invoice period + credit buffer) we can accept for migration windows.

Sarah — would you be OK with us returning a marked-up Exhibit E with proposed language by EOD tomorrow? If that still looks good we can schedule a short call Friday to close.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exhibit pricing — sequencing & true-up questions

Folks — reviewing Sarah's asks and Sean's notes. High-level legal position and proposed redline snippets below:

1) Order of precedence (binding sequence) — Proposed snippet: "In the event of any inconsistency between the Order Schedule and an Exhibit, the Order Schedule shall govern with respect to SKU-level definitions and billing mappings; the Exhibit shall govern with respect to pricing guardrails (caps, floors, and stabilizers) unless the parties expressly state otherwise in a signed amendment."

Rationale: gives deterministic rule while preserving Exhibit E as the source of pricing mechanics.

2) True-up cadence — We can accept quarterly true-ups. Proposed snippet: "True-ups shall be conducted on a quarterly basis and any shortfall shall be calculated pro rata for the applicable quarter. For avoidance of doubt, quarterly true-ups will apply the floor pro rata for that quarter (i.e., floor * (days in quarter / 365))."

Comment: Karthik to verify the floor math; if finance wants to keep annual floor equivalency we can add a note to scale the per-quarter floor accordingly.

3) Billing mapping during migration — Proposed fallback language: "If usage in an invoice period spans multiple SKU families due to an authorized migration event, parties shall apply the mapping provided in the Order Schedule for the first invoice in which both SKUs appear; any discrepancies identified within 60 days may be resolved via invoice credit not to exceed the pro-rated overlap volume."

I've attached a short PDF with inline comments (Exhibit_E_markus_comments.pdf). I tried to keep language narrow and operational. If the customer accepts these three snippets, we should be able to produce a marked Exhibit E for signature.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Exhibit_E_markus_comments.pdf

Subject: Re: Exhibit pricing — sequencing & true-up questions

Markus / Sean — thanks for the quick review and concrete snippets. Novus legal reviewed the proposed wording and we can accept the binding-sequence and true-up snippets as-is. A few quick points:

- Billing mapping fallback: we agree to the 60-day reconcile window but ask that the credit cap be expressed as "not to exceed the pro-rated overlap volume or $5,000, whichever is greater" for small-dollar migrations to make remediation meaningful.

- Implementation note: can Redwood publish a short ops runbook (1-pager) describing how the quarterly true-up will be calculated and what invoice metadata Novus should expect? That will speed our internal approvals.

If you can incorporate the $5k language and provide the ops runbook link we will circulate for final signature. I've attached a final redline (Exhibit_E_v4_final.pdf) with our acceptance marks.

Happy to take the 20-min call Friday at 10:00 PT if you prefer to walk through the runbook together.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Levin
Sr. Procurement Manager, Novus Health
